newsitem.title: USA: Cahners Business Confidence Index 66.2 in July.
newsitem.headline: Cahners Business Confidence Index 66.2 in July.

text.p: The Cahners Business Confidence Index (CBCI) fell 0.4 of a point to 66.2 in July versus June, Cahners Economics said.
"July's decline indicates that the business sector has bought into the belief that growth will slow over the remainder of this year," the Cahners report said.

Four of the seven CBCI components fell in July. Modest increases were seen in marketing spending at 1.8 points, capital spending at an increase of 0.2 points, and research and development spending at 0.5 points.
The employment component fell by a half point in July, although remaining above the CBCI average for the month.
The highest levels of optimism were centered in the electronics industry, and the Western region of the U.S., according to the report.
The Electronics Industry Business Confidence was 68.4, off 0.4 from June, but still above industry-wide average, it said.
"Nearly 90 percent of respondents from the electronics industry have made a substantial investment in new technology - the largest share of the four industries," the report said.
